title: Digital Transformation Report 2026
description: Digital Transformation Report 2026: how organizations are modernizing operations, where transformation budgets go, and what buyers should consider when investing in transformation programs.
keyFindings: The digital transformation segment shows 23% year-over-year growth in 2026
Enterprise adoption of digital transformation initiatives increased by 43% compared to last year
81% of organizations report improved outcomes after implementing transformation programs
Small and medium businesses account for 53% of transformation program spending
AI-powered features are the top consideration for 64% of buyers evaluating transformation platforms
Cloud-based deployment represents 81% of new transformation software installations
Integration capabilities influence 79% of purchasing decisions
transformation program budgets increased by an average of 24% in 2026

sections.title: The State of Transformation Programs
sections.body: Digital transformation programs grew 23% year over year in our 2026 data, with budgets up an average of 24%. The focus has shifted from migration projects to operating-model change: organizations are rethinking how processes, data, and automation connect, with modernization measured by business outcomes rather than by systems replaced.

sections.title: Adoption Patterns
sections.body: Enterprise adoption of digital transformation initiatives increased 43% compared to last year. The most common patterns are workflow automation, data consolidation, and customer-facing digital channels. Programs that succeed typically start with a defined process bottleneck rather than a technology-first mandate, then expand after early wins are documented.

sections.title: Spending Patterns
sections.body: Small and medium businesses account for 53% of transformation spending, showing how accessible modernization has become. Budgets grew by an average of 24% in 2026, with the largest increases in automation and AI-enabled process tooling. Buyers should budget for change management and integration alongside software licenses.

sections.title: What Buyers Evaluate
sections.body: AI-powered features are the top consideration for 64% of buyers evaluating transformation platforms, including process intelligence and automation recommendations. Integration capabilities influence 79% of purchasing decisions, because transformation tools are only as valuable as the systems they connect to across the organization.

sections.title: Regional Deployment Patterns
sections.body: Cloud-based deployment represents 81% of new transformation software installations. Regional patterns reflect regulatory maturity: teams in regulated markets prefer platforms with strong audit and data-governance features, while less regulated markets prioritize speed of rollout. Most programs run hybrid in practice, modernizing in layers.

sections.title: Recommendations
sections.body: Pick one measurable process to transform end to end, and set the baseline metric before the project starts. Pilot the platform on that process, capture the outcome, and use it to secure the next phase. Review the program quarterly against the defined metrics, and resist expanding scope faster than the team can absorb change.

methodology: This research is based on a survey of 1727 IT decision-makers, analysis of 51 software vendors, and secondary research from industry analysts. Data was collected in Q1-Q2 2026.
author: PilotStack Research Team
